commands: Build etlantic, etlantic-prefect, etlantic-sql, etlantic-sqlmodel, etlantic-fastapi, and the separate worker-plugin wheels; install them into a new Python 3.11 environment from locked requirements.

ETLANTIC_CP_TEST_URL=postgresql+psycopg:///postgres ETLANTIC_PHASE058_INSTALLED_BACKEND_PLUGIN=1 env -u PYTHONPATH /tmp/phase058-route-cleanup-venv/bin/python -m pytest -o pythonpath= -q tests/prefect -m prefect
result: Installed-wheel Prefect/PostgreSQL suite: 43 passed in 52.01s with no skips. Installed-wheel headless/FastAPI route parity: 1 passed in 0.54s.
assertions: All five ETLantic package imports and the separate worker-backend plugin resolve from the newly built wheels in the isolated Python 3.11 environment, with PYTHONPATH unset and pytest's configured pythonpath disabled.

The Prefect suite includes live PostgreSQL multiprocess retirement followed by deletion of an unused exact Prefect deployment; it also covers cleanup refusal for retained route references, retention denial, cleanup-pending reactivation fencing, and retry after a lost delete response.
Managed schedule creation reserves its execution route durably; route retirement remains blocked until the schedule is deleted through the schedule service, which releases the reservation.
The live campaign overrides the 30-day minimum retention to zero seconds to keep the test bounded; it confirms the exact deletion path but does not establish elapsed production retention.
The installed FastAPI/headless parity test preserves equivalent managed-route semantics across both submission surfaces.
A frozen-clock test denies cleanup one second before the default 30-day retention cutoff and allows the cleanup attempt at the exact cutoff; the live deletion keeps its bounded zero-second override.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised API process backed by per-test PostgreSQL databases
runtime.worker_backend_plugin: Separately built and installed etlantic-phase058-test-worker-plugin 0.1.0 wheel

source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted repository-relative source paths and file bytes, with NUL separators.
limitations: This is a local installed-wheel campaign, not remote CI evidence or a production support commitment.
Only CPython 3.11.15, Prefect 3.7.8, PostgreSQL 16.13, and the Process pool were exercised; other versions, operating systems, hosting modes, and work pools remain unqualified.
The real 30-day retention interval has not elapsed; the live cleanup test uses a zero-second test override.
The full phase release decision remains open, including remote CI, the complete support matrix, broader server fault/recovery, and independent production connector conformance.

ci_configuration.database_service: Local PostgreSQL 16.13; test-owned rows and dedicated Prefect databases were cleaned by fixtures.
ci_configuration.server_process: Separate Prefect API process with PostgreSQL persistence

cleanup: The suite used unique route, tenant, workspace, deployment, and database identities; fixture-owned SQLModel state and dedicated Prefect databases were removed after each test.
The shared local PostgreSQL service and temporary installed-wheel environment were left intact; per-test Prefect API processes were stopped.
